summary.text: 事 is an early picture of a hand holding an unidentified object. The character is attested for duties or office, events, and serving; its common current meanings include matter and affair. The evidence does not establish a single path linking these uses.

formation.text: Pictographic: the early graph depicts a hand holding something. Proposed identifications of the object include a flag, document container, brush, or implement, but none is established. A later dictionary analysis divides 事 into 史 and abbreviated 之 as a sound element; this does not establish the formation of the early graph.

components.text: The early graph is a whole picture of a hand holding an unidentified object. Competing proposals identify the object as a flag, document container, brush, or implement; it is not securely identified.

history.text: Paleographic accounts describe 事, 史, 吏, and 使 as forms differentiated from an earlier shared graph showing a hand holding something. Records list oracle-bone, bronze, Chu manuscript, small-seal, and Shuowen form categories, but do not date the first individual specimen. The selected seal-script image is a modern redraw of a received form, not an ancient artifact.

The received Shuowen analysis treats 史 as the meaning element and abbreviated 之 as a sound element. This later analysis differs from the account of related graphs differentiating from a shared earlier form; it does not establish the components of the early graph.

uncertainties.text: The held object’s identity and name remain disputed. Because its name and pronunciation are not established, a sound-based borrowing from that object’s name is not demonstrated.
The examples attest several uses but do not establish a complete chronology or a single semantic path connecting them.

senses.text: Bronze-inscription examples attest 事 for duty or office. The cited examples do not establish this use as earlier than the other attested uses.

senses.period: Bronze inscriptions and early texts; exact dates unresolved
senses.text: Bronze inscriptions attest an event sense, and cited early-text examples use 事 for matters or events. The evidence does not establish priority among these uses.

senses.period: Bronze inscriptions and early texts; exact dates unresolved
senses.text: Bronze examples attest a command or service use; cited early-text examples also attest serving and undertaking. They do not establish a linear development from duty or event.
Current uses include affair, matter, and business.

limitations.text: The cited examples support multiple uses but do not establish the original spoken word’s precise meaning or a chronological chain among the attested senses.

overview.text: 事 pictures a hand holding something, though the object is disputed. Early inscriptions use it for duty, events, and serving; today it commonly means “matter” or “affair.” The evidence does not show how these meanings developed from one another.

components.text: The whole early picture shows a hand holding an object; proposals for what it was remain disputed.
